transcript_body:
MEETING HEADER:
Date: 2026-11-26
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Lina Park (Redwood SE), Ben Ortiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Eileen Carter (Nimbus ML Lead), Marco Reyes (Nimbus Platform), Olivia Zhang (CTO), Samir Das (SRE)

SUMMARY (auto): Quick signal snapshot across INT8/FP8 variants. INT8 shows 12-18ms/token savings in our runs but median quality drift ~2.3% on the 1k eval set; FP8 shows smaller latency wins but better fidelity. Discussed KV cache and prefix effects and an ops playbook for canary + rollback.

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run 50 minutes ish, agenda is signal snapshot tldr, then ops playbook, then owners.
[00:22] Dr. Eileen Carter: cool, our team is excited to see the latest numbers, we had week-on-week noise but wanted a consolidated view.
[00:35] Lina Park: quick note - we re-ran the 1k eval with same prompts, INT8 baseline used our quant profile A, FP8 used blend profile B. We also ran with and without KV cache.
[00:48] Marco Reyes: when you say "KV cache" is it cold starts only or warm prefixes? we care about chat workloads where prefix reuse is high.
[00:53] Lina Park: both; we included a 1000-warm-prefix microbench and a cold-start sample; warm prefixes show >2x throughput improvements with KV cache turned on.
[01:12] Ben Ortiz: numbers - on A100s with our runtime: INT8 median token latency down ~18ms/token (seq len 128), throughput +28% at 4 concurrent streams; FP8 was around 9-11ms/token improvement and throughput +15%.
[01:39] Olivia Zhang: ok but what about quality numbers, can you quantify regression?
[01:46] Lina Park: yes, on the 1k eval set (mix of instructions, summarization, QA), INT8 had an aggregate quality delta of -2.3% (we measured an MRR-like score and a hallucination flag rate). FP8 was -0.6% on same metric. Not uniform — some prompt buckets (long-form summarization) saw 4-6% delta.
[02:10] Dr. Eileen Carter: 4-6% on long-form is concerning, that triggers product risk for us. What's the plan?
[02:17] Jordan Kim: that's expected — blend/precision-sensitive buckets will need either fallback or canary gating. Today's ops playbook proposal: default to INT8 for throughput-sensitive routes, enable FP8 or full precision for long-form and a canary that checks quality metrics in real time.
[02:42] Marco Reyes: can we do per-route routing? our infra can tag routes by intent, yes. we'll need model-variant mapping.
[02:48] Ben Ortiz: yep Redwood routing supports per-route model pinning and auto-fallback. We can map route -> model_variant; we also suggest a small scoring lambda that computes an SNR-like metric on responses and signals drift.
[03:06] Samir Das: about the SLOs, our latency SLO is 250ms p95; what's p95 change when you switch to INT8?
[03:13] Lina Park: on seq len 128, p95 improved from 310ms to 255ms with INT8 + KV cache; without KV cache it's closer to 275ms. FP8 p95 is 270ms. So INT8+cache meets 250-260 range but depends on real prefix reuse.
[03:36] Dr. Eileen Carter: interesting, that may meet ops if we ensure higher reuse; many of our chat sessions have long-lived contexts so should be ok.
[03:45] Olivia Zhang: any regressions in deterministic outputs like exact-match for QA tasks?
[03:52] Lina Park: exact-match dropped ~1.8% in INT8 overall but for short QA it's smaller ~0.5%. Long-form generation accounts for bulk of drift.
[04:05] Jordan Kim: to be conservative we propose this playbook: 1) roll INT8 to low-risk routes (short answers, embeddings), 2) route long-form to FP8, 3) run a canary 100rps for 1 hour with Delta checks (SNR, hallucination rate, exact-match), 4) automatic rollback threshold at >2.5% quality delta on the monitored set.
[04:35] Marco Reyes: who owns the monitored set? we want reproducible tests.
[04:39] Lina Park: Redwood can maintain the 1k eval canonical set and share CSVs; Nimbus must run KV-cache microbench and confirm infra numbers.
[04:47] Dr. Eileen Carter: can you share raw diff CSVs? we need to inspect edge cases where INT8 flipped answers.
[04:54] Jordan Kim: yes action item, we'll send raw outputs and per-case diffs.
[05:01] Ben Ortiz: small gotcha - INT8 sometimes changes tokenization boundaries in our toolchain, so we included token-level edit distance to help triage.
[05:12] Samir Das: security/obs question: if we do private deployment, do audit logs include per-token model variant? we need to prove which variant served which request.
[05:22] Lina Park: Private deployment includes request-level routing metadata and model variant field; audit logs are configurable and can be forwarded to your Kinesis/CloudWatch. We also support KMS key integration for encryption at rest.
[05:38] Olivia Zhang: great. Also curious about cost delta — do you have unit economics for INT8 vs FP8?
[05:44] Jordan Kim: rough numbers: INT8 reduces GPU spending by ~22% in our runs due to higher throughput and lower memory footprint; FP8 about ~12% saving vs FP16. Exact savings depend on batch sizes and utilization.
[06:03] Dr. Eileen Carter: pricing will be a big factor. We'll want to model 3-month spend projections if we adopt INT8 for 40% of traffic.
[06:12] Jordan Kim: we can run a cost model once bench numbers + traffic split are provided.
[06:18] Marco Reyes: on the canary, what exact metrics are we going to compute?
[06:22] Ben Ortiz: propose: p95 latency, median token latency, hallucination rate (human-simulated flags via eval set), exact-match delta, and an SNR proxy (embedding similarity to reference). If any cross threshold, automated route flips back to FP8 or full precision.
[06:43] Lina Park: also recommend sampling 1% of requests for full-precision back-check in the canary window to catch edge regressions.
[06:50] Dr. Eileen Carter: that helps. How long to run KV-cache microbench — we can do it in a day?
[06:55] Lina Park: yep microbench is quick; we'll provide a script. Marco, if you run it overnight you'll have numbers tomorrow.
[07:03] Marco Reyes: ok will pick it up.
[07:06] Jordan Kim: other blockers?
[07:10] Olivia Zhang: we need the raw diffs to do product sign-off. Also an ops playbook doc for rollback steps.
[07:16] Ben Ortiz: we'll draft the playbook and include commands and monitoring dashboard links.
[07:21] Jordan Kim: let's recap actions — Lina share eval CSVs and microbench script, Ben draft rollback playbook, Marco run KV bench and schedule canary, Jordan will send cost model template.
[07:36] Dr. Eileen Carter: timeline — aim to have canary week of Dec 6, 1-hour window, then follow-up to validate.
[07:45] Jordan Kim: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll circulate notes and attach the CSVs.
[07:52] END OF TRANSCRIPT

NOTES:
- Raw outputs will include per-case diffs and token-level edit distance to speed triage.
- Suggested automated rollback threshold: >2.5% aggregate quality delta on canonical set or >5% in any critical bucket.
- Canary config: 100rps sustained for 1 hour with 1% of responses run through FP16 back-check sampling.
